subject: Pajama "Sunrise Screenings" of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
query: why are people wearing pajamas to sunrise on the reaping
title: Why are people wearing pajamas to Sunrise on the Reaping? Dawn shows
answer: Because the studio asked them to. Lionsgate is holding special "Sunrise Screenings" of "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" early on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, and the official Hunger Games TikTok invited fans to come in their pajamas, turning the movie's title into a literal early-morning outing.
body:
The pajama posts you're seeing are tied to a real event, not a random joke. "Sunrise on the Reaping," the prequel that follows a young Haymitch Abernathy through the 50th Hunger Games, opened in U.S. theaters on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. For the next morning, Lionsgate scheduled "Sunrise Screenings" timed around dawn at more than 130 theaters, including AMC, Regal, Cinemark and some regional chains. The official Hunger Games account then posted a TikTok telling fans to wear their pajamas to get "the full sunrise experience." Fans now use it as a dress code: "PJs, blanket, 6 a.m. Reaping, let's go" is the general idea.

The theme lands with longtime fans for a second reason. In November 2015, Woody Harrelson, who played the adult Haymitch in the original films, showed up to a Paris photocall for "Mockingjay – Part 2" in a T-shirt, plaid pajama pants and socks, a moment that still circulates online. Some fans at early showings have dressed up as Harrelson's pajama look, a nod to the character the new film is about. In the prequel, Haymitch is played by Joseph Zada.

It spread this week because it's easy to join: everyone already owns pajamas, the screenings are on a weekend morning, and "what I wore to the sunrise showing" videos double as opening-weekend reviews. Searches like "why is everyone wearing pjs to Sunrise on the Reaping" started climbing on Nov. 19, the day before release. Exact start times vary by theater, and some locations add extras such as coffee, breakfast or collectible pins while supplies last, so check your local listing.

For parents: this is a harmless, opt-in fan event. Pajamas are not required at any showing, and regular screenings run all weekend. The film itself is a Hunger Games story about a deadly televised competition, so check the rating and reviews before bringing younger kids.

faq.a: No. It's an optional theme for the special morning shows. Regular screenings have no dress code.
